In one sentence: manufacture, assemble, install, maintain, and repair boilers, tanks, and large vessels to drawings, with the core being reading drawings, forming, joining, aligning, checking fit, and keeping records. The U.S. counterpart is 47-2011.00, usually entered through apprenticeship. In mainland China, an operator's inspection records are not the same as a statutory inspection agency's supervisory inspection conclusion; design appraisal and construction notification obligations for boilers must be verified by equipment and process.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to read the drawings and process documents before starting work; you can wear protective equipment as required and accept inspection by the foreman and safety officer at heights, in confined spaces, and near noise and high temperatures; when you find problems with welds, tube expansion, or accessories, you are willing to stop and report first rather than getting it running first; and your interest in under what operating conditions a part fails and how large the consequences are exceeds your interest in how fast you worked today.

Pause major investment first: if you do not yet understand drawings, tolerances, processes, and safety requirements, complete the paper exercises on this page first and then verify courses and qualifications with formal practical training or an apprenticeship program. Short-term training, knowing one welding method, or passing a simulated exercise does not prove that you can independently take on pressure equipment manufacturing, installation, or inspection signing.

Verify education, qualifications, and authorization separately. The United States usually requires a high school diploma or equivalent, and BLS lists a typical 4-year apprenticeship; welding or related experience may give priority or shorten the apprenticeship. Some states require a boilermaker license, usually including experience and an examination, and employers may require or prefer professional certification; verify with the target state and employer. The general training description for O*NET Job Zone 1 to 2 cannot replace this trade's 4-year apprenticeship pathway. Mainland China personnel qualifications should be verified by actual work and current assessment items, and not all auxiliary assembly positions can be uniformly required to hold the same certificate. Special equipment welding and emergency management special operations fall under different rules; from August 2026, TSG Z6002—2026 is implemented, and those who already hold a valid special equipment welding certificate but no welding and thermal cutting operation certificate must take the hot work assessment under the new rules at expiry review or when adding items, while employers must still strengthen hot work safety management in the meantime.

In one sentence: this is a skilled trade centered on drawing interpretation, metal assembly, welding and joining, pressure test support, and on-site installation and maintenance safety, and its output is traceable physical work and records that meet design and safety technical specifications, not design review conclusions or inspection report signing. The U.S. wage, employment, and projections data follow the precise Boilermakers (SOC 47-2011) occupation definition; mainland China has no national occupation-level wage statistics corresponding to this occupation, and this page marks this honestly rather than filling in figures.

The work of boilermakers falls into three categories: first, manufacturing and assembly tasks (reading drawings and laying out, cutting and forming, aligning and securing structural members, rolling and bending, expanding or welding tube ends, and installing manholes, handholes, nozzles, and valves); second, on-site installation and repair tasks (rigging and positioning heavy plates and frames, assembling large vessels on site, repairing or replacing safety valves and regulators, straightening deformed plates, and building furnace refractory); third, inspection and record tasks (assisting with pressure tests, checking welds and accessory defects, cleaning and maintaining equipment, and filling in work and inspection support records to procedure). All three share the same traceable safety and quality chain.
Manufacturing and assembly tasks

Read drawings to determine positions, relationships, and dimensions → mark cutting and bending lines → form and machine components → align and secure structural members or plates → perform expansion, riveting, or welding and other joining → check fit and weld quality → deliver the assembled component or vessel.
On-site installation and repair tasks

Verify the site foundation and datum points → rig and position the component in coordination with rigging signals → assemble large vessels or frames on site → connect piping and accessories → repair or replace defective components and straighten deformation → build refractory → perform pre-restart checks and hand over records.

Assist with pressure tests on boilers and other vessels, inspect assembled vessels or individual components (tubes, accessories, valves, control mechanisms, and auxiliary machinery) for defects, identify leaks, weak points, or defective sections, direct the cleaning of boilers and furnaces, and report immediately when accident hazards or unsafe factors are found and take effective measures to safety to ensure safety in accordance with operating procedures.

Boilermakers work around the manufacture, assembly, installation, and repair of boilers, tanks, and vessels; plumbers (47-2152.00) work around piping systems, welders (51-4121.00) work around joining processes, sheet metal workers (47-2211.00) focus on thin-sheet products, structural iron and steel workers (47-2221.00) work on building structures, and millwrights (49-9044.00) work on machinery installation and alignment. Tasks may overlap, and it cannot be asserted that welders never take on assembly or that sheet metal workers never touch other components; responsibility, training, and work qualifications must still be verified by position.
Core purpose

Manufacture, install, and maintain boilers and pressure vessels to design and safety technical specifications so that they operate safely, reliably, and traceably under pressure and high-temperature conditions.
Main subjects and basis

The subjects are boilers, tanks, vessels, pressure vessels, piping and accessories, and refractory materials; the basis is drawings and design documents, safety technical specifications and standards, welding and assembly process procedures, and on-site safe work and protection requirements.
Core process

Reading drawings and laying out, cutting and forming, assembling and aligning, joining (welding, tube expansion, or riveting), rigging and positioning, pressure testing and defect inspection support, and recording and handover.
Main outputs

Components and vessels that meet drawings and specifications, systems installed, positioned, and connected, equipment after repair and straightening, and traceable work records and inspection support records.
Responsible party

Work inspection and records are completed by authorized operations and quality personnel; statutory supervisory inspection is carried out by approved special equipment inspection agencies to the specifications. The scope of design document appraisal should be verified against the equipment listed in Article 20 of the Special Equipment Safety Law, and not all design checks should be written as statutory appraisal.
Permissions and approval

Mainland China: Article 18 of the Special Equipment Safety Law provides for production licensing; Article 20 states that design documents for boilers and similar equipment must be appraised by an approved inspection agency before being used for manufacturing, and this does not cover all pressure vessels uniformly; Article 23 requires written notification before installation, modification, or repair work; Article 25 provides for supervisory inspection during the manufacture of boilers and pressure vessels and the installation, modification, and major repair of the listed equipment; Article 14 requires personnel qualifications to be verified under relevant national provisions, and Article 24 requires technical materials to be handed over within 30 days after acceptance. Welding, rigging, work at heights, and confined space protection should be verified separately by actual risk, work category, and site rules.
Conclusion boundaries

Work inspection only states the result for this component within the verified process and coverage and does not replace the overall equipment conformity or supervisory inspection conclusion. Article 41 of the Special Equipment Safety Law requires operators to report immediately when they find hazards or unsafe factors; safety management personnel have the right to decide to stop use and report when they find an emergency. Specific work stoppage, resumption, and release must be verified under the applicable procedures and authorization, and each defect should not automatically be turned into an individual statutory right to stop the whole unit.

Before starting, verify at least six items: the position definition and unit qualifications, the apprenticeship or training pathway, the actual processes and equipment used, personal work qualification and certificate requirements, safety protection arrangements for heights and confined spaces, and the real pay method and working hours.
Occupation definition

Mainland China positions must be verified by equipment catalogue, actual process, the unit's licensed scope, and personnel assessment items; manufacturing, installation, welding, maintenance, and operations positions cannot be exchanged merely on the basis of the name boiler worker. Occupational classification, education and training, and individual work permits are different concepts, and this page does not claim one-to-one correspondence with U.S. 47-2011.
Education and training pathway

The United States usually requires a high school diploma or equivalent, and BLS lists a typical 4-year apprenticeship; welding or related experience may give priority or shorten the apprenticeship. Some states require a boilermaker license, usually including experience and an examination, and employers may require or prefer professional certification; verify with the target state and employer. The general training description for O*NET Job Zone 1 to 2 cannot replace this trade's 4-year apprenticeship pathway. Mainland China personnel qualifications should be verified by actual work and current assessment items, and not all auxiliary assembly positions can be uniformly required to hold the same certificate. Special equipment welding and emergency management special operations fall under different rules; from August 2026, TSG Z6002—2026 is implemented, and those who already hold a valid special equipment welding certificate but no welding and thermal cutting operation certificate must take the hot work assessment under the new rules at expiry review or when adding items, while employers must still strengthen hot work safety management in the meantime.
Methods and tools

The detail page lists 8 software categories, and a separate Hot single page lists 7 products: AutoCAD, Outlook, SAP, Office, Windows, Excel, and Word; the job posting shares are in the AI section. The 8th category is computer-assisted training software, and no health and safety product name was confirmed from the page. Mechanical tools and on-site operations must not be conflated with software categories; a software label does not prove automation, individual mandatory training, or quality authorization.
Safety and work permits

The work involves heights, confined spaces, rigging, high temperatures, and noise; verify the provision and inspection requirements for personal protective equipment (safety shoes, goggles, gloves, hearing protection, hard hat, and respiratory protection and safety harness where necessary), hot work and confined space permits, and on-site emergency and evacuation arrangements.
Construction notification and inspection support

Mainland China: Article 18 of the Special Equipment Safety Law provides for production licensing; Article 20 states that design documents for boilers and similar equipment must be appraised by an approved inspection agency before being used for manufacturing, and this does not cover all pressure vessels uniformly; Article 23 requires written notification before installation, modification, or repair work; Article 25 provides for supervisory inspection during the manufacture of boilers and pressure vessels and the installation, modification, and major repair of the listed equipment; Article 14 requires personnel qualifications to be verified under relevant national provisions, and Article 24 requires technical materials to be handed over within 30 days after acceptance.
Pay and working hours

When comparing positions, verify hourly pay, piece-rate or project pay, overtime calculation, travel and accommodation arrangements, and work arrangements after the contract ends. BLS notes that there may be idle periods when on-site contracts end, and that overtime may occur during shutdown maintenance or delivery phases; this page does not assume all positions have site allowances.

Boilermakers (U.S. counterpart O*NET-SOC 47-2011.00, Boilermakers) manufacture, assemble, maintain, and repair stationary steam boilers and boiler house auxiliary equipment to drawings; align structural members or plates to assemble boiler frames, tanks, or vessels; use hand and power tools, plumb bobs, levels, wedges, clamps, or turnbuckles; assist in testing assembled vessels; direct the cleaning of boilers and furnaces; and inspect and repair boiler accessories such as safety valves, regulators, automatic control mechanisms, water level indicators, and auxiliary machinery. It is not a purely manual material handling position, and the official task definition does not automatically confer design or inspection signing qualifications; taking on such positions elsewhere requires verifying qualifications and authorization independently.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET-SOC 47-2011.00 Boilermakers, page updated 2026, Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), and this occupation is not marked Bright Outlook. The official duty is to manufacture, assemble, maintain, and repair stationary steam boilers and boiler house auxiliary equipment; there are 18 tasks, and the high-importance tasks include conducting pressure tests on boilers and other vessels (78), studying drawings to determine positions, relationships, and dimensions (77), inspecting boilers and pressure vessels to locate defects (73), inspecting assembled vessels and components for defects (71), and laying out and marking bending and cutting lines (69).

U.S. wage distribution: the 2025 BLS occupational employment and wage statistics (OEWS) shown by O*NET, under the precise Boilermakers (SOC 47-2011) occupation definition — annual wage 50,490 USD at the 10th percentile, 64,760 USD at the 25th percentile, 76,410 USD at the median, 95,430 USD at the 75th percentile, and 110,370 USD at the 90th percentile; the corresponding median hourly wage is 36.74 USD. The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook gives the May 2025 median annual wage as the same 76,410 USD.

Mainland China side: the National Bureau of Statistics 2025 average annual wages of urban unit employees (released 2026-05-15) publishes average wages by industry category and broad job category but does not list the boilermaker occupation separately; this page therefore provides no mainland China wage figures for this occupation and keeps only the statistical definition and gap explanation. Work involving boilers and pressure vessels is governed by the Special Equipment Safety Law of the People's Republic of China.

Both the current O*NET and BLS give 2025—2035: 10,200 employed in 2025 and 10,100 in 2035, a decline of 2%, with 700 annual openings; the BLS table lists a net change of -200, and the endpoints and change are rounded separately, so they cannot be subtracted directly to replace the table values. BLS explains that the openings all come from replacement demand due to transfers or exits and are not equal to 700 net new positions.

O*NET2025 U.S. Boilermakers industry distribution: construction 60%, manufacturing 14%, and other 26% (including other services and mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction). This is the industry distribution of the occupation, not industry wages, a Chinese distribution, or an individual employer assignment.

paragraphs: This page compares boilermakers with five adjacent trades on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and output, key differences, and which direction better fits each preference. Adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean trade names are interchangeable.

Evidence note: the career directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 47-2011.00 and the related occupations list, under the U.S. definition; the qualifications and work permits of adjacent trades must be verified separately by their own jurisdictions, work involving pressure parts has additional supervisory inspection requirements, and this page does not write any direction as a shortcut for a career change.

The table below compares boilermakers with adjacent trades and the pathways for moving in from adjacent positions; the basis for judgment is the main output, the object of responsibility, and the required training, not how similar the trade names are.
Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters (47-2152.00)
Install, maintain, and repair water, heating, gas, and steam piping systems, with outputs mainly being piping systems and connections.

Both involve piping and connections, but boilermakers center on boilers, tanks, and pressure vessel bodies and must handle thick-walled pressure parts, tube expansion, and pressure test support; plumbers focus on piping system layout and usually do not manufacture vessel bodies.

If you want to work around piping systems and equipment connections, consider plumbers first; if you want to handle the manufacture, assembly, and pressure joining of vessel bodies, consider boilermaking first.
Welders, Cutters, Solderers, and Brazers (51-4121.00)
Center on the joining process itself, completing welding, cutting, soldering, or brazing to process procedures.

Welders take welding, cutting, and brazing and other joining processes as their main responsibility; boilermakers also handle reading drawings, positioning, assembling, maintaining, and test support for vessel components. Specific positions may overlap, and it cannot be asserted that welders never take on assembly.

If you would rather focus on welding processes and quality, consider welders first; if you are willing to take on assembly and on-site positioning responsibility at the same time, consider boilermaking first.
Sheet Metal Workers (47-2211.00)
Fabricate and install thin sheet metal products such as ductwork, metal roofing, and enclosures.

Sheet metal workers mainly fabricate and install thin sheet metal products; boilermakers work with boilers, tanks, large vessels, and thick metal parts. The two differ in material and output emphasis, and tolerances cannot be compared or all overlap ruled out merely on the basis of the name.

If you would rather do thin sheet forming and building installation, compare sheet metal workers first; if you want to do the manufacture and assembly of thick-walled pressure structures, consider boilermaking first.
Structural Iron and Steel Workers (47-2221.00)
Install structural steel beams, columns, and related components for buildings, with outputs mainly being building structure installation.

Both involve rigging and joining heavy metal parts, but structural iron and steel workers work on building structures while boilermakers work on pressure equipment, which requires completing joins to safety technical specifications and supporting supervisory inspection.

If you would rather do structure and rigging on construction sites, consider structural iron and steel work first; if you want to handle the manufacture and installation of pressure equipment, consider boilermaking first.
Millwrights (49-9044.00)
Disassemble, reassemble, calibrate, and maintain industrial machinery and equipment, primarily to restore equipment condition and precision.

Millwrights work around the installation and alignment of machinery and equipment and do not necessarily handle pressure parts; boilermakers must master the joining processes and test support requirements for pressure structures.
If you would rather work around machinery precision and repair, compare millwright work first; if you want to handle boiler and pressure vessel bodies, consider boilermaking first.
Moving in from building installation or manufacturing positions
You already have welding, steel structure installation, fitting, or equipment repair experience and want to move toward pressure equipment.

The gap is usually not physical effort or tool use but drawings and tolerances, pressure structure processes, pressure test support, and special equipment qualification and notification requirements; being able to weld is not the same as being able to independently take on pressure part work.

If you are willing to build up drawing, process, and safety specification training and accept the qualification requirements, you can consider moving in; if you only want to change the job name without building up specifications and qualifications, the gap will be large.

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main output, the object of responsibility, and the required training, not how similar the names are; once the direction is set, verify item by item the target trade's training and qualification requirements, the actual processes and equipment used, safety protection arrangements for heights and confined spaces, and the unit licensing and personnel qualifications where special equipment is involved, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Students or career changers preparing to enter this occupation

First complete the paper dimension, deviation, and record exercises on this page, and then verify formal apprenticeship or practical training arrangements. Working boilermaking and installation personnel

Editorial task analysis: use digital tools for reviewable steps such as reading drawings and process documents, cutting and layout calculations, welding material and labor hour statistics, and arranging inspection records; assembly tolerance judgment, joining process selection, safety protection, and anomaly handling must remain with people.

paragraphs: Boundary: this section describes occupational risks and responsibility boundaries, not an evaluation of any individual or institution; specific legal duties and handling processes are determined by the applicable jurisdiction, the construction unit, and the institutional authorization chain.

Direct answer: main risks include falls during work at heights and in confined spaces, crushing and collision from rigging and heavy components, high temperatures and hazardous gases, fire and burns from welding and cutting, dust and noise exposure, inadequate pressure part joining or inspection support, and missing construction notification and supervisory inspection steps; control depends on work permits, safety briefings, personal protective equipment, and traceable records.

Evidence scope: the risk and boundary entries are based on the official tasks, work activities, and work context of O*NET 47-2011.00, the O*NET training and education information, the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, and public materials from the Special Equipment Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA); they do not cover the internal rules of specific institutions.
Operators, work teams, and the construction unit
Falls, crushing, burns, or poisoning can cause serious injury and lead to work interruption and accountability.

Responsible personnel should verify permits, isolation, protection, monitoring, and rescue arrangements by jurisdiction, space risk, and work category. U.S. construction confined spaces follow OSHA1926.1203, distinguishing general spaces from permit-required spaces; not all height or confined space activities should be treated as the same permit.
Permit, isolation, protection, monitoring, or rescue conditions that should be verified by law or site rules have not been implemented; entering a permit-required space without authorization.

Defects in pressure part joining or assembly may fail during operation, causing equipment damage and personal injury.
Work to drawings and process procedures, keep joining and inspection records, support supervisory inspection, and rectify as required.
Welding without process qualification or parameter verification, or failure to repair defects found in inspection as required.
The construction unit and the equipment user

In China, production of applicable equipment should be undertaken by a licensed unit; equipment within the scope of statutory supervisory inspection must not leave the factory or be delivered if it has not been inspected or fails inspection. Unit production licensing and equipment inspection results are two separate obligations, and the equipment itself cannot be described as lacking production licensing.

Mainland China: Article 18 of the Special Equipment Safety Law provides for production licensing; Article 20 states that design documents for boilers and similar equipment must be appraised by an approved inspection agency before being used for manufacturing, and this does not cover all pressure vessels uniformly; Article 23 requires written notification before installation, modification, or repair work; Article 25 provides for supervisory inspection during the manufacture of boilers and pressure vessels and the installation, modification, and major repair of the listed equipment; Article 14 requires personnel qualifications to be verified under relevant national provisions, and Article 24 requires technical materials to be handed over within 30 days after acceptance.
Engaging in production without obtaining a license, failing to perform construction notification, or leaving the factory or delivering for use without supervisory inspection.
Operators and employers
Performing the relevant work without the required qualifications may lead to being ordered to correct the situation and to bearing liability.

Qualifications of personnel in mainland China should be checked against the actual work and current assessment items, and not all auxiliary assembly positions should be required to hold the same certificate. Special equipment welding and emergency management special operations fall under different rules; TSG Z6002—2026 takes effect from August 2026, and those who hold a valid special equipment welding certificate but no welding and thermal cutting operation certificate must take a hot work assessment under the new detailed rules when their certificate is due for review or when new items are added, and employers must still strengthen hot work safety management in the meantime. Order No. 19 of the Ministry of Emergency Management has been in force since 2026-06-01; for the special operations it covers, personnel must be trained and assessed and hold an operation certificate before working, and where other departments have other provisions, those provisions apply.

values: Fictional paper-based drawing-reading package

All editor-created, all units in mm: rectangular plate outline L=500±1, W=300±1; the lower left corner is the origin, hole A center (x=50±0.5, y=40±0.5), hole B center (x=450±0.5, y=40±0.5), and the horizontal center distance between the two holes is Bx−Ax=400±0.5. Each limit includes its endpoints. Check only these dimensions; no material, welding method, or pressure design is provided.

Initial measurement M1: L500.6, W298.8, Ax50.2, Ay39.7, Bx450.9, By40.1. Revision M2 changes only Bx to 450.4; M3 then changes W to 300.2, with all other values unchanged. The revisions are fictional re-measurement data, do not require actual machining, and M1 must not be crossed out.

The only tools are pen and paper, a calculator, or a local spreadsheet; 120 minutes: 30 minutes to draw the sketch and the upper and lower limits, 45 minutes to record and judge three times, 25 minutes for the exception report, and 20 minutes to check against the answer. Actual cutting, welding, lifting, entering vessels, or pressure testing are prohibited, and no practical training station or outside personnel are needed to complete it.
Dimension judgment and delivery

Draw a sketch with the origin and units, list the upper and lower limits for L/W/Ax/Ay/Bx/By and the horizontal distance, and for M1, M2, and M3 fill in the measured value, the deviation (measured − nominal), and pass or pending item by item; calculate the horizontal distance as Bx−Ax and do not confuse it with the diagonal distance. If any item fails, that round is "dimensions pending"; only when all pass is it "dimension check passed".

Submit the three-round dimension tables, the exception report, and the revision records, and state which round can be called dimension check passed, and why it cannot be called manufacturing qualified, welding qualified, or pressure safe. The exception report lists the drawing version SIM-01, the record versions M1/M2/M3, out-of-limit items, review requests, and items to be confirmed; do not change drawing limits on your own.
Reference answer and review

Ranges: L[499,501], W[299,301], Ax[49.5,50.5], Ay/By[39.5,40.5], Bx[449.5,450.5], horizontal distance [399.5,400.5]. The M1 deviations are, in order, +0.6, −1.2, +0.2, −0.3, +0.9, +0.1, and the horizontal distance is 400.7 with a deviation of +0.7; W, Bx, and the horizontal distance fail, the rest pass, and the whole round is pending.

M2: Bx450.4 passes with a deviation of +0.4, and the horizontal distance is 400.2 with a deviation of +0.2, which passes; W is still 298.8 and fails, so the whole round is still pending. M3: W300.2 passes with a deviation of +0.2, the other values are the same as M2, and all seven items pass. You may only write "the dimensions listed in SIM-01 pass the dimension check"; keep the three rounds of data and the two revision reasons, and note that material, joint quality, measuring tool calibration, and real safety are all unverified.
Exercise limitations

The tolerances in the problem are only fictional exercise conditions and are not boiler or pressure vessel design standards. This exercise involves no physical objects, welds, pressure, or compliance certification, and a matching answer does not create a work qualification or release authority; real processes are carried out only under formal training, applicable qualifications, and position authorization.
Position requirement checklist

List the target jurisdiction, equipment, process, education and training, individual assessment items, unit licensing, and authorization; attach a source, a data period, and items to be confirmed to each.
Do not mix apprenticeship completion, a special operations certificate, a special equipment welding qualification, and unit licensing into the same status.
Three-round dimension review
Attach the SIM-01 sketch, the M1/M2/M3 seven-item table, and the three-round conclusions, compare item by item with this page's reference answer, and note the differences.

You can review it yourself; if you ask a master to review it, record the real feedback separately; if there is no external review, state clearly that you did not obtain one, as it does not block the paper exercise.
Exception and revision report
Report the three out-of-limit items in M1, that the width still fails in M2, and that the dimensions listed in M3 pass, and keep the original records and the two revision reasons for Bx and W.
This only explains the dimensions in the problem; it cannot sign off manufacturing qualification, welding qualification, an inspection report, or pressure release.
Reproduction and decision

Attach the input data, calculation formulas, tables, or paper trail; if you use AI, record the scope of assistance and the manual corrections, and finally write whether to continue, build basics, or compare adjacent positions.
Note that material, welds, measuring tool calibration, and on-site risks are unverified; do not upload real drawings and do not touch real equipment.

Read O*NET and BLS, write the differences between manufacturing, installation, repair, and operations positions, and attach sources and jurisdiction.
Problem statement and scope
Copy the SIM-01 dimensions, tolerances, and origin and M1—M3, calculate the seven upper and lower limits, and draw the sketch.
Initial measurement judgment

Revision re-measurement
Calculate M2 and M3; explain why M2 still cannot be written as dimension check passed, and keep the two revisions and the original measurements.
Answer review
Check item by item against this page's answer, correct formula or unit errors, and save the before-and-after differences; no hands-on machining or mentor appointment is needed.
Qualifications and portfolio

Organize the three-round tables and the exception report, and list the qualification and unit licensing verification questions for the target position; you may ask a master to review them, and note it if you could not arrange one.
Investment decision

Decide whether to continue, build basics, or switch direction based on how complete your records are and how you feel about drawing reading, checking, and error correction; also check the cost, courses, and qualifications of formal practical training, as passing on paper does not mean actual competence.

entries: Continue: if you can complete the three-round dimension tables and are willing to accept checking and error correction, you can go on to consider a formal apprenticeship or practical training.
Build basics: if you repeatedly make mistakes with units, deviations, or ranges, first improve your drawing reading and basic calculations.
Switch direction: if you would rather study operating parameters, mechanical calibration, or sheet metal products, compare the corresponding adjacent positions.
Check qualifications: verify individual items, unit licensing, and position authorization according to the actual equipment, process, and jurisdiction.
Keep the portfolio: save the sketch, the three-round tables, the exception and revision records, and the limitation note together.
Assess costs: check formal training fees, work hours, tools and protection, and out-of-town construction arrangements, and do not promise income based on numbers on the page.

Next step: based on genuine verification, decide whether to sign up for a formal apprenticeship, build basics, or explore an adjacent direction; do not enter real hazardous processes without qualifications and authorization.

The United States usually requires a high school diploma or equivalent, and BLS lists a typical 4-year apprenticeship; welding or related experience may give priority or shorten the apprenticeship. Mainland China: Article 18 of the Special Equipment Safety Law provides for production licensing; Article 20 states that design documents for boilers and similar equipment must be appraised by an approved inspection agency before being used for manufacturing, and this does not cover all pressure vessels uniformly; Article 23 requires written notification before installation, modification, or repair work; Article 25 provides for supervisory inspection during the manufacture of boilers and pressure vessels and the installation, modification, and major repair of the listed equipment; Article 14 requires personnel qualifications to be verified under relevant national provisions, and Article 24 requires technical materials to be handed over within 30 days after acceptance. entries.answer: The risks to watch for in advance include falls from height and in confined spaces, crushing and impact from lifting and heavy parts, high temperatures and hazardous gases, fire and burns from welding and cutting, dust and noise exposure, inadequate connections or inspection cooperation on pressure parts, and missing construction notification and supervisory inspection steps; control depends on work permits, safety briefings, personal protection, and traceable records.

entries.answer: Fit signals are being able to read drawings and complete assembly and connection within tolerances, being willing to follow safety rules and report problems honestly, and accepting quality inspection and rework; an interest in machinery or tools alone is not enough to prove competence.
